chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man: does anything cut off his prayer from what passes in front of him? He said: Nothing cuts off the prayer of a Muslim, but ward off what you can.

He said: And I asked him about a man who had a nosebleed, and his nosebleed did not stop until the time for prayer entered. He said: He should stuff his nose with something, then pray, and not prolong (the prayer) if he fears the blood will overtake him.
He said: And he said: When you turn your head in an obligatory prayer before completion, repeat the prayer if the turning is excessive; and if you have already performed the Tashahhud, do not repeat.
ai.seo_question: What breaks the validity of Islamic prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that minor distractions like passing objects do not invalidate the prayer, reflecting the Shia principle of ease (yusr) in worship, while providing a pragmatic solution for nosebleeds that prioritizes completing the obligatory act. The ruling on turning the head distinguishes between significant deviation (which requires re-prayer) and minor movement, emphasizing that intention and degree of distraction determine validity rather than rigid physical stillness. This hadith is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for understanding the boundaries of nullifiers (mubtilat) versus mere detractors of concentration (khushu).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the man, can anything cut off his Salāt, from what passes by in front of him?’ So heasws said: ‘Nothing cuts off a Salāt of the Muslim, but safeguard as much as you can’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about a man with nose-bleed, but his nose-bleed did not flow until the time for Salāt came up. Heasws said: ‘He should stuff his nose with something, then he should pray Salāt, and he should not prolong (the Salāt) if he fears the blood to flow’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And heasws said: ‘When you turn in a Obligatory Salāt from other than completion, so repeat the Salāt, when the turning was unreasonable; and if you had performed Tashahhud, so do not repeat’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man whose Salah (prayer) is discontinued because of something passing in front of him. He (the Imam) said, ‘Salah (prayer) of a Muslim does not become discontinued by anything; however, protect as much as you can.’

He (the narrator) has said, ‘I then asked him (the Imam) about a man who experiences nose bleeding which does not stop until the time of Salah (prayer). He (the Imam) said, ‘He fills his nose up with something, then performs Salah (prayer), but does not take a long time if he fears bleeding.’

He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) said, ‘If he experiences nose bleeding in obligatory Salah (prayer) without break he performs his Salah (prayer) again if he has turned away from al-Qiblah (al-Ka’bah) before completing. If he has said Tashahhud (testimonies of belief), then he is not required to perform again.’”
